source.title: Analysis of DAWNBench, a Time-to-Accuracy Machine Learning Performance Benchmark
source.authors: Cody A. Coleman; Daniel Kang; D. Narayanan; Luigi Nardi; Tian Zhao; Jian Zhang; Peter D. Bailis; K. Olukotun; Chris Ré; M. Zaharia

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including tables, figures, and conclusion.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates whether benchmark-optimized models generalize to new data using held-out image and translation datasets; this is a conceptual test of generalization, not a memorization-capacity experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unseen-data accuracy for optimized entries and reference models. It does not test fitting random labels, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer comparisons, dropout, sharpness measures, or removing memorized examples. Large-batch results describe throughput and convergence, not a controlled comparison of test error at fixed epoch budgets.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates time-to-accuracy as a benchmark metric and checks whether benchmark-optimized models retain accuracy on new data. None of these comparisons tests V1–V8. It cites optimizer generalization differences and reports batch-size-dependent epochs to target accuracy, but does not compare optimizers or held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets. Generalization alone does not establish any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that TTA is usually stable and that models optimized for TTA generalize nearly as well as standard or reference models. Their conclusion also emphasizes substantial hardware underutilization. The unseen-data comparisons concern overall optimized recipes and establish none of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes benchmark entries with heterogeneous training recipes and evaluates them on new data; it does not reproduce the cited memorization or gap-measurement methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that Flickr images are not entirely representative of ImageNet and reports different accuracy metrics for image-classification entries; image results span different architectures and hardware configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: On newly collected Flickr images, optimized image classifiers attained accuracies close to the pretrained ResNet-50 reference. Optimized GNMT and Transformer models scored 23.63 ± 0.20 and 26.78 ± 0.45 BLEU, versus reference scores of 23.44 ± 0.08 and 26.60 ± 0.44.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models optimized for time-to-accuracy can retain comparable performance on additional unseen evaluation data in the tested image-classification and translation settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 7 reports that larger-scale, larger-batch entries require more epochs to reach the target quality: Transformer 2 to 6, GNMT 3 to 5, ResNet 63 to 82, SSD 49 to 55, and Mask R-CNN 13 to 14. Hardware scale and potentially other recipe choices also change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Throughput speedups can overstate time-to-accuracy speedups because larger-batch distributed training can require additional epochs to reach a fixed quality target.

record.problems: The Flickr images are described as not entirely representative of ImageNet and cover 886 of 1000 classes. The accuracy comparisons use pretrained ResNets as references, not matched models trained under a control recipe. The paper does not report training errors for the evaluated checkpoints, so it cannot establish training-test gaps or the capacity to fit random labels. Translation results average three runs and report standard deviations.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Batch-size/epoch/throughput entries in Table 7 do not report held-out accuracy under fixed epoch budgets, so they do not qualify for V5 rows.

untested.parts: No random-label training, memorization-capacity measurement, or paired natural-label/random-label evaluation.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison; the optimizer generalization difference is cited background.
No comparison of held-out performance between batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, or controlled test of remedies. Table 7 reports epochs needed to reach a quality target instead.
No dropout ablation or comparison involving removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with generalization gaps.
No identification or removal of memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change V5 from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. Table 7 is already declared in rows_left_out and does not warrant a missing-result entry. Training-test gaps are unnecessary for several listed versions; the decisive issue here is the absence of their required experimental comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label generalization.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison.
Reports batch size, epochs, throughput and time-to-accuracy, but does not report the version’s fixed-epoch comparison of held-out performance between large and small batches.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
Does not identify or remove memorized examples.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses optimizer and batch-size effects on generalization using prior work, but the study's own comparisons do not test any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates benchmark stability, unseen-data performance of optimized recipes, and hardware utilization. None tests or uses V1–V8; batch-size comparisons measure epochs to target accuracy rather than held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Flickr images are explicitly not entirely representative of ImageNet; these overall recipe comparisons establish none of V1–V8.
